claims.text: The initial cold-rolled Cantor-type CoCrFeMnNi alloy has high residual stress.
The initial cold-rolled alloy has a heterogeneous microstructure.
Controlled recrystallization heat treatment reduces residual stress in the cold-rolled alloy.
Controlled recrystallization heat treatment homogenizes the alloy's grain structure.
Residual-stress reduction promotes formation of a more uniform passive oxide film.
Residual-stress reduction promotes formation of a more adherent passive oxide film.
The improved passive film repassivates mechanically abraded areas more rapidly.
Rapid repassivation counterbalances passive-oxide removal during sliding.
Faster repassivation reduces synergistic degradation from combined wear and corrosion.
Recrystallized samples will exhibit faster repassivation than cold-rolled samples.
Recrystallized samples will exhibit lower corrosion current densities than cold-rolled samples.
Recrystallized samples will exhibit lower wear volumes than cold-rolled samples.
Cold-rolled samples have less consistent passive-film formation than recrystallized samples.
Cold-rolled samples undergo greater tribo-corrosion degradation than recrystallized samples.
The predicted benefit should hold under moderate chloride exposure and moderate sliding stress when repassivation kinetics dominate.
Extreme mechanical loads may overwhelm repassivation and eliminate the predicted benefit.
Highly aggressive corrosive environments may eliminate the predicted benefit because film removal or degradation outpaces film formation.
The degradation reduction may vary nonlinearly with the degree of residual-stress relief.
Annealing-induced microstructural changes other than residual-stress relief may affect repassivation and degradation.
